focused_acceptance.reason: On PDF pp.20-21 the normalized matrix has determinant (s^2-4)/(t^2-4). With sigma=2,t=4,s=7 the true adjugate product is [[22,-60],[1,0]], while (72) prints [[23,-60],[1,0]]; these nonsingular matrices are not projectively proportional. Independently, an explicit proper binary octahedral subgroup H of SL2(F97) has |H|=48, |H'|=24 and |H''|=8, refuting the all-proper-subgroups metabelian premise. Proposition 14 feeds Corollary 15 and the main proof, so this is Major under the core-proof criterion. Bourgain's primary text says large proper subgroups, and the paper offers alternate Corvaja-Zannier/Stepanov routes. These limit the impact; no main-theorem counterexample or complete subgroup replacement is claimed.

focused_acceptance.reason: Corollary 21 on PDF page 29 only excludes the identity PGL2 map. Inversion permutes all t roots of unity; choose arbitrarily large t and a prime p=1 mod t with p>t^(4/3). The intersection then has size t, contradicting a uniform O(t^(3/4)) bound. The preceding proposition's disjoint-divisor hypothesis excludes inversion, and the actual b!=0,1 application avoids this degeneracy. This is a local unrestricted-statement defect, Minor, rather than demonstrated failure of the principal theorem.
